subject: gl2genepop() heterozygote REF/ALT allele assignment issue - dartR v2.0.4

messages.author: 01668e867549c468
messages.subject: gl2genepop() heterozygote REF/ALT allele assignment issue - dartR v2.0.4
parts:
Hi! Thanks for all the great work you are doing with dartR!

This is an issue that may not have any real world implications but would be best practice and would facillitate genotype validation.

I notice that dartR:gl2genepop() exports heterozygote alleles without regard to placing the REF allele first and then the ALT allele second.  This can be seen here (see attchment) for loci 1056834-46-T/C,414328-16-C/T,1020344-60-A/G,761770-16-T/C,455852-24-G/A (see attachment).

Firstly, GENLIGHT locus coding is: 0 - Homozygous reference allele, 1 - Heterozygous, 2 - Homozygous alternate allele, NA - Missing. NOTE: this different to Dart coding:"0" = Reference allele homozygote, "1" = SNP allele homozygote, "2"= heterozygote and "-" = double null/null allele homozygote (absence of fragment with SNP in genomic representation)

Now the issue. For GENLIGHT matrix values of 1 (heterozygous) the REF/ALT allele order is not exported. I assume the allele REF/ALT order should corespond to the locus name. For example, locus 1056834-46-T/C has REF/ALT alleles of T/C. For the GENLIGHT matrix (attachment pg 2, mtx_gl_filt) the value of this locus for sample 2480939 = 1 and I would expect alleles to be coded as 0203 which is the case (see attachment pg2, gl2genepop() output file sample NSW_2480939, first locus) . However for locus 414328-16-C/T the REF/ALT alleles are C/T, and alleles are exported as 0203 rather than 0302 as per my assumption (and best practice?). The same issue occurs for the other loci when they are heterozygous, however, homozygote alleles are exported with regard to REF/ALT alleles exactly as I would expect.

See the attachment for examples. Apologies for the pedantry! Thanks for your time.

Cheers,

Dean

messages.author: 592079bda2cb3220
messages.subject: Re: gl2genepop() heterozygote REF/ALT allele assignment issue - dartR v2.0.4
parts:
Hi Dean,

Thank you for your detailed description of the issue.

I have modified the gl2genepop function, so the REF and ALT alleles are now ordered as in the locus name.

The updated version of the function is available in the developing version of dartR and can be installed by typing in the R console:

> gl.install.vanilla.dartR(flavour = "dev")

Cheers,
Luis
